newsitem.title: FRANCE: BHV saw improved sales in April.
newsitem.headline: BHV saw improved sales in April.

text.p: French department stores group BHV said on Monday its sales improved in April, offsetting in large part the poor sales seen in February and March.

The improvement was, however, slightly artificial as the company had brought forward promotional activity to start in April, chairman Jean-Pierre Boulot told an analysts meeting. He gave no sales figures, nor gave a profit forecast for 1997.
BHV reported a 1996 net attributable profit of 56.5 million francs, versus 48.5 million in the prior year.
It expects to spend around 80 million francs and at least the same amount for 1998 in investments, Boulot said.
That compares with BHV's nearly 40 million francs in investment in 1996.
The group had net cash of 821 million francs at the end of December, compared with 760 million in 1995.
BHV wants to open a 7,000 square metre store in the Lebanon in the middle of next year, Boulot said. It would be its first outlet overseas.
If the results met expectations, it could open a second store in that country but the priority remained sales in France, particularly Paris, he said.
